key_insight: SymFT speeds up fault-tolerant quantum circuit simulation by separating symbolic Clifford/Pauli frame effects from the few operations that actually change sampling probabilities, while adapting stabilizer coordinates to minimize per-shot work.
engineering_relevance: This makes large-scale simulation of error-corrected and near-Clifford circuits more practical for benchmarking, protocol design, and performance analysis on standard CPU hardware.
method: Symbolic Clifford–Pauli frame factorization: treat residual Clifford/Pauli frames and sign-flipped noise/feedback symbolically so they do not need to be applied every shot.
Adaptive stabilizer-coordinate planning: use a shared stabilizer–destabilizer tableau to define a basis and keep only active non-stabilizer degrees of freedom in a compact dense vector.
Direct multi-coordinate sampling: resolve basis changes once and generate sampling instructions without per-shot tableau updates or localization-induced Clifford transforms.
evidence_signal: In the abstract’s evaluation, SymFT outperforms Stim by 2.51–2.56× on surface-code circuits, Clifft by 1.86–3.51× on magic-state cultivation/distillation circuits, and exceeds the authors’ prior SOFT simulator by over two orders of magnitude on tested cultivation circuits.
watch_item: The approach depends on careful symbolic bookkeeping and adaptive basis management, so implementation complexity and correctness of frame/coordinate updates are important concerns.
paper_title: SymFT: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuit Simulation via Symbolic Clifford--Pauli Frames and Stabilizer Coordinates
